title: The Devil's Bath
review: I liked how they portrayed the people of 1750 like they really were: very similar to us. Movies would usually have you think they only talked about kings and wars, but in reality they talked about their jobs, finances, gossip, relationships and hobbies. This isn't a very fun time, but it looks beautiful and it's effective at protraying the slow creeping misery that the protagonist feels. It's one for enjoyers of serious arty films, and grounded realistic folk horror. The obvious comparison is {Hagazussa: A Heathen's Curse}, and if you like one then you'll like the other. Damn it must have been cold in the evenings. I suppose they went to bed much earlier than I do, and they probably took fewer hot showers too.
